explanation: In a still fluid the pressure grows with depth because every layer carries the weight of all the fluid stacked above it: P = Patm + rho·g·d. Move the depth dot down and watch P climb linearly — each extra meter of water (rho = 1000 kg/m³) adds rho·g ≈ 9800 Pa. The four green arrows show that fluid pressure pushes EQUALLY in all directions at a given depth, not just downward. Denser fluids build pressure faster with depth.
bullets: Pressure rises linearly with depth: P = Patm + rho·g·d.
At any point the pressure pushes equally in every direction.
Only depth matters — the shape or width of the container does not.
